title: personal-experiment-tracker-llm-tuning-mini-sheet
content:
Experiment tracker (personal) — mini-sheet

Purpose: quick, personal tracking for small LLM tuning runs, cost estimates, and notes to self. Not official.

Columns:
- date
- exp_id
- model
- dataset
- prompt_change
- lr
- batch
- steps
- eval_metric (accuracy / ROUGE)
- tokens_used
- est_cost (USD)
- status
- notes

Recent runs (CSV-style rows for quick copy/paste):
2025-11-05, exp-001, gpt-small-v1, internal-summaries-v1, add "keep bullets" instruction, 2e-5, 16, 2000, acc=0.72, tokens=45k, $3.40, done, baseline
2025-11-12, exp-002, gpt-small-v1-int8, internal-summaries-v1, quantize int8, 2e-5, 16, 2000, acc=0.69, tokens=42k, $2.80, in_progress, small quality drop vs float32
2025-12-01, exp-003, gpt-small-v1, internal-summaries-v2 (noisy), prompt: add temp filter, 1e-5, 32, 1500, acc=0.74, tokens=38k, $2.90, done, better generalization
2026-01-10, exp-004, gpt-medium-v1, internal-summaries-v1, prompt v1 + system role, 1e-5, 8, 3000, rouge-L=0.58, tokens=120k, $9.60, ab_test, slower but higher quality
2026-02-20, exp-005, gpt-small-v1, internal-summaries-v1, enable prefix cache, 2e-5, 32, 2500, acc=0.73, tokens=60k, $4.50, running, expect lower latency

Quick cost heuristics and notes:
- Dev run cost estimate = (tokens_used / 1000) * unit_cost; target dev unit_cost <= $0.08 per 1k tokens for baseline jobs.
- Prefer batch 16/32 for throughput; watch latency for canary tests.
- Int8 quantization reduces token cost ~15-25% but need to verify quality on eval set.
- Use eval-set-A (200 examples) for quick regressions + 20 manual spot checks.

Action items / next steps:
- 2026-02-28: run exp-006 with batch=32 + prefix cache enabled + int8 to validate cost/quality tradeoff (owner: me)
- Add small eval script to repo: scripts/eval_quick.sh (TODO: push PR)
- Capture per-run latency percentiles (p50/p95) next run and add column to sheet

Snippets (save for quick reruns):
- Finetune: python run_finetune.py --model gpt-small-v1 --lr 2e-5 --batch 16 --steps 2000 --data data/internal-summaries-v1 --out runs/exp-002
- Eval: python eval.py --model runs/exp-002/checkpoint --data eval/eval-set-A.json --metrics accuracy,rouge

Handy links:
- Confluence notes: confluence:PROD-LLM-TUNING
- Jira ticket: JIRA-ENG-1823
- PR with preprocessing changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/models/pull/42

Notes to self:
- Keep this mini-sheet light — migrate important experiments to the team tracker once promising (threshold: eval_metric >= 0.75 or cost reduction >20%).
- When confident, create a short run-book for reproducibility (params, seed, dataset snapshot).

(End of mini-sheet)
